newsitem.title: UK: UK bank lending rose 3.066 billion stg in October.
newsitem.headline: UK bank lending rose 3.066 billion stg in October.

text.p: Total sterling lending by major British banking groups to the UK private sector rose a seasonally adjusted 3.066 billion stg in October, the British Bankers' Association (BBA) said.
This was up from the September figure of 2.403 billion but close to the six-monthly average of 2.959 billion.
Consumer credit rose by 507 million stg against 411 million in September and compared with a six-monthly average of 434 million.
Mortgage lending rose by 625 million stg compared with 416 million and 571 million respectively.
Lending to the manufacturing sector rose by 442 million stg, while lending to the financial sector fell by 445 million, ending a run of eight monthly rises.

BBA director-general Tim Sweeney said strong credit demand from the personal sector was a feature in October, with mortgage lending bouncing back and consumer credit demand continuing very buoyant. "With the financial sector repaying funds in October, the other factor behind the growth of the major banks' lending was a greater and more widespread appetite for finance by industry and commerce, whose borrowing rose by some 1.5 billion stg," he said.
